en: The Legend of the Elder Amodaphaliya Kaṇikāra Chapter, Number Eight I was once a tree-spirit dwelling in a forest grove, And I saw the Buddha, the Great Sage, the One with Vision, The Teacher who had arrived at the foot of the Rose-apple Tree. Having seen him, I offered a *amoda* fruit to the Blessed One. Because of that root of merit, I have never fallen into the lower realms; For twenty thousand eons I dwelt in the world of the gods. From there, passing through various celestial abodes, I attained the state of a Wheel-turning Monarch. In my final existence, I was born into a wealthy family; I was handsome, virtuous, and possessed of great splendor. I gave alms-food to the Buddha Kassapa, And I took refuge in the Three Jewels. Having performed such deeds, I passed away from that life And was reborn in the realm of Tusita. There I enjoyed divine pleasures for ten thousand eons, And then I attained the state of a Universal Monarch. Having passed away from that life as well, I was reborn here in this human world. I am now the Elder Amodaphaliya, A disciple of the Buddha Gotama. Through the power of that deed, My body is fragrant and delightful. Even when I walk upon the earth, The ground becomes fragrant for a league around. When I enter a city or a village, The fragrance spreads throughout the entire town. Even those who are far away, Smell the scent as they approach me. This is the fruit of giving alms-food, And of taking refuge in the Triple Gem. May all beings attain such a state, And may they reach the blissful city of Nirvana. Thus ends the legend of the Elder Amodaphaliya.
The fruit that gave me joy:
that fruit which I gave back in the ninety-first aeon;
I do not recognize a state of misery;
this is the fruit of giving fruit.
The defilements have been burnt away by me.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Amodaphaliya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Amodaphaliya is the eighth.
